title.narrative: Enhanced Vocational Education and Training Project II

description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives are to improve equitable access to market relevant training programs and to strengthen the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector service delivery in Nepal.

The development objective of Second Enhanced Vocational Education and Training Project for Nepal are to improve equitable access to market relevant training programs and to strengthen the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector service delivery in Nepal. This project has two components. 1) The first component, Support to Results-based Financing, aims to finance results in the TVET sector that are related to the achievement of the PDO. It has the following subcomponents : (i) Strengthening Service Delivery in Technical Education, which has the following sub results area sub components (a) Quality Improvement Grants for Technical Education; (b) Improving Management, Instructor and Assessor Quality; and (c) Modernizing Technical Education Curricula. (ii) The second sub component, Widening Access to TVET Programs, has the following sub results area sub components: (a) Pro-poor Scholarships for TSLC/Diploma Students; (b) Performance-based Funding of Short-term Vocational Training Programs; and (c) Testing of prior skills (TOPS). (iii) The third subcomponent, Pilots in Enabling Youth Transition to Work has the following sub results area sub components: (a) Apprenticeship Programs; and (b) Placement Services. 2) The second component, Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, has the following subcomponent, (i) Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation; and (ii) Sector-wide initiatives.

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall carry out the Project, and shall cause the Beneficiaries to implement their respective activities/Institutional Development Plans under the Project, in accordance with the PIM.

The Recipient shall maintain the Project Implementation Committee (“PIC”), chaired by the Secretary, MOE, consisting of,inter-alia, officers of the Ministry of Education, Council of Technical Education and Vocational Training, National PlanningCommission and of other ministries and departments of the Recipient, responsible for guiding and overseeing Project implementationbased on selected assignments set forth in detail in the Project Implementation Manual (PIM), including: (i) the review of Projectannual work plans and budgets prepared by the PS; (ii) the coordination among the ministries and government agencies receivingsupport from the Project; and (iii) the monitoring of Project implementation progress and outcomes.

The Recipient shall maintain the Project Secretariat (“PS”), headed by a Project Director and staffed with professionals, all ofwhom shall have qualifications, experience, and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, which PS shall be entrustedwith the day-to-day implementation of the Project, including, inter-alia, the planning, budgeting, coordination, procurement,financial management, auditing, and monitoring and evaluation of Project activities.

The Recipient shall, not later than sixty (60) days after the Effectiveness Date, adopt a Project Implementation Manual (PIM)issued by the PS and endorsed by the PIC, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

The recipient shall ensure, and cause the Beneficiaries to ensure, that the Project (including any activities carried out under theQuality Improvement Grants) is implemented in accordance with: (i) the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF,including the Vulnerable Community Development Framework (VCDF)); (ii) the Environment Management Plan(s) (EMP), and/or thevulnerable communities development plans(s) (VCDP) to be prepared, as the case may be, in accordance with the objectives, policies,procedures, time schedules and other provisions set forth in the ESMF (the ESMF, VCDF, EMP(s), and VCDP(s), collectively referredto as the “Safeguards Instruments”.
